source.title: Generalization and Overfitting in Matrix Product State Machine Learning Architectures

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some mathematical notation is flattened or garbled, but the results and figures are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly sweeps MPS bond dimension and training-set size, and reports cases with overfitting as well as cases without double descent. Its results qualify the generality of the claim and emphasize dependence on data and architecture.
record.gate_note: Rows record the authors’ own MPS results on artificial data and MNIST. Values are mostly qualitative because the curves are plotted rather than tabulated. Cited results from other studies are not recorded. The full-MNIST training-accuracy result is mentioned as not shown and is not a row.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps capacity (MPS bond dimension), training-set size and label noise in matrix product state models, a non-deep-network model class. It reports test-loss and test-accuracy curves that bear on whether a double-descent peak and second descent appear. This is a new setting with direct results on the claim (V3, V4, V6). V1 is restricted to deep networks, so it is untested here.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. The authors also speculate that the difference arises because the artificial data is effectively one-dimensional, which suits an MPS, while MNIST is two-dimensional. They note they may have overshot a narrow double-descent range of χ, but judge it unlikely to occur at much larger χ.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines MPS regression and classification by varying bond dimension, using inversion and compression or DMRG optimization. It does not reproduce the original deep-network experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with data type and complexity (artificial data versus MNIST; ε), training-set size, and label-noise condition.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal bond dimension χ* increases with training-set size and with data complexity ε. Exceptions are ε=0.4 and ε=0.8, which do not follow this trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In MPS models, the capacity that minimizes test error grows with the amount of signal in the data (sample count and target complexity).

record.problems: Most plotted outcomes are not given as exact numerical values. Artificial-data results are averaged over 100 data sets for inversion/compression and 32 for the reported DMRG comparison; the MNIST sample-size result is described as somewhat noisy. The authors note that the tested bond-dimension range may miss a narrow feature, and that larger bond dimensions and other data sets require investigation.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying own results were omitted. The paper mentions full-MNIST training accuracy as not shown, so it is not recorded as a row. Results attributed to cited studies are excluded.

untested.parts: All of V1: the study uses only MPS tensor networks, not deep networks.
All of V2: test error is never reported as a function of epoch.
All of V5: no single effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested.
Multiple or triple peaks, and whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak. L2 is fixed at 10^-6 for the artificial data.
All of V7: there is no re-expression of the results in terms of an effective number of parameters.

missing.what: Figure 4 and Figure 8 DMRG results for ε=0.3, 0.4 and 0.8 (U-shapes, plus a mismatch between the two methods at small χ). Also the Appendix D exceptions at ε=0.4 and ε=0.8, which do not follow the χ* trend.
missing.locator: Section III, Figure 4 bottom panel; Appendix D, Figures 7–8

record.verdict_notes: The rows were moved from V1 to V4 because MPS models are not deep networks. The reversed states were changed to absent, since monotonic improvement is a lack of the effect rather than its opposite. No row reports numeric values; all states rest on the authors' descriptions of the plotted curves.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests MPS bond dimension, not size sweeps in other deep-network architectures. In its artificial-data cases, it reports an overfitting upturn but does not report a subsequent second descent.
The paper reports results after specified training durations and longer MNIST optimization, but does not measure test error as a function of training epoch to test a fall-rise-fall curve.

The MNIST sample-size sweep is reported at fixed bond dimension, but does not establish behavior for all data types or specifically characterize a narrow interval around the interpolation threshold in the artificial-data experiments.
The study evaluates MPS architectures only; it does not test a general double-descent curve across model classes.
The study does not propose or test a single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study tests training-label noise on MNIST and reports no double descent. It does not test multiple or triple peaks, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes a peak.
The study does not re-express its results using an effective number of parameters or test whether that converts a second descent to an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: MPS
rows.size_stated: Bond dimension χ varied; target MPS maximum bond dimension χ=27 at the center bond for N=6 and f=3.
rows.operation_detail: Sweep MPS bond dimension and training-set size using inversion followed by compression.

conditions.value: artificial data generated by a target MPS

rows.value: The authors report a best-generalizing finite bond dimension χ* when the training set does not fully specify the weight tensor; χ* increases as the number of training samples increases. They report nearly perfect performance for Ntr≥729.
rows.uncertainty: One standard deviation across 100 training data sets; plotted values not stated.
rows.note: The text describes a finite-dimension test-loss minimum and subsequent degradation, but does not report a later second descent. The training-size sweep is not a direct isolated test of whether adding data raises test error at a fixed model size.
rows.check: MPS is a tensor-network model, not a deep network, so the link belongs on V4 rather than V1. The U-shaped test loss is observed up to χ=27, the bond dimension that fits the data exactly, but no second descent is reported. The V3 link is removed: the Ntr sweep is not reported as test loss at fixed χ against sample count.

source_check.notes: The authors allow that a narrow peak could have been skipped and recommend larger bond dimensions and other datasets. χ=27 denotes full representational capacity for the artificial setup, not an independently measured training-interpolation threshold.

statements.correction: MNIST; Ntr=1024; χ∈[2,20]; 0%, 10%, 20% randomly corrupted training labels; 800–2000 epochs depending on condition; no double descent reported. Added corruption is insufficient to produce a peak in these experiments. Peak causation, multiple peaks, and optimally tuned regularization are not established.
statements.problem: The MPS results and conditions are accurate, but insufficient noise-induced peak formation does not contradict V6's claim that noise or variance drives an existing peak.
